Do you hear that? The constant gunfire? The shelling? And they tell the world there is a ceasefire? There is no pause. No reprieve. No safety for Palestinians in Gaza. On October 11, our team visited families whose tents had been burned, leaving them without shelter once again. Even as we filmed, heavy gunfire echoed around us. This is the reality of life in Gaza. Families who have lost everything continue to live under the threat of violence, yet refuse to be driven from their land. This is what steadfastness looks like. Sumud. A determination that is difficult to comprehend unless you understand what it means to face the loss of your homeland. They have burned their shelters, destroyed their neighborhoods, and displaced them again and again. But they have not broken their connection to Palestine. They are not leaving. They are not surrendering their right to exist on their land. Help support them. The Sameer Project is one of the only organizations that delivers aid in these danger zones. Give to our Food and Water Campaign .

Heavy rain swept through tents sheltering displaced Palestinians in Gaza City on Saturday, leaving families wading through water around their shelters. The flooding is making daily life increasingly difficult for people in the camps, who are now facing a third winter there. "This is the first day of rain, and of course we are already flooded," said Olfat El-Magdoub, a displaced Palestinian sweeping water from her tent. She said that when it rained two weeks ago she spent four days sleeping on blankets on the floor because the bedding was soaked. Rafiq Ghattas, who lives in the Mina camp, home to around 1,700 families, said conditions deteriorated within an hour of the rain starting. Palestinian authorities say more than 74,000 people have been killed in Gaza since the conflict began on October 7, 2023. #Gaza #GazaCity #Flooding #DisplacedPalestinians #Palestine #Winter #MiddleEast #CGTNEurope

In Gaza, winter means being displaced all over again. Today on November 7, heavy rains in Gaza City completely submerged Yasser’s family tent. The mattresses they slept on were soaked. Every piece of clothing inside, including the children’s clothes, was wet. Their family had already been displaced. Now the tent they depended on for shelter is gone, too. And this is the case now for over 150,000 families. While so many of us are warm and dry, children in Gaza are watching floodwater seep into the places they’re supposed to sleep. How is it acceptable that a family can lose everything, start over in a tent, and then lose what little they have left in a single night? Please give to The Sameer Project’s winter campaign in our General Fund. Families need dry bedding, warm clothes, and shelter from the rain now.

Macklemore says nine major US arenas have refused to host his Free Palestine benefit shows. The rapper says venues pulled out after learning the concerts would raise money for organisations supporting Palestinians. They include New York’s Madison Square Garden and the Barclays Center, as well as venues in Los Angeles and San Francisco. He says that in more than 20 years of touring, he’s never experienced anything like it. But Madison Square Garden has pushed back, saying it has limited availability and that Macklemore is not an arena-level act. The rapper says he plans to continue organising shows for Palestine. #politics #macklemore #edsheeran
